items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: I went with another guy that used to play. His name was Meade, Will Meade. He was an awful good professor.

ctx.x: Well, who is the gentleman that taught you how?

Well, the man that I first started with was Dave Perkins. And ever since Dave Perkins, I went with another guy that used to play. His name was Meade, Will Meade. He was an awful good professor. Well, now that's been some years ago. He had a cigar stand on Royal and Espenade. That's where I used to go to. He was a mighty nice musician too.
Jack, how far from this section that we are right now have you lived? Have you always lived in this neck of the woods? Well, Doctor, fortunately I did.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1957-03-26
items.q: my boy, practicing and wanting it on this fellow, Mead and Perkins, pulled him through.

ctx.x: Was Vega a ragtime player or what did you

read on it? Oh, very good ragtime player. Very good. Very good. Yeah. In fact, as I'm telling you, well, him and Manuel Marlowe, in fact, were the first two kids that I picked up on horn. Then I began to get my boy, my boy, practicing and wanting it on this fellow, Mead and Perkins, pulled him through. And then got Johnny Lawler and boys like that in another place. Well, Brunus and all, they used to be with me all the time, the Brunus boys. The Brunus boys, especially Georgie Brunus, Georgie Brunus never left my…
Did they play regular cornets in those days or were they different?
